title: Seeing basic shapes
summary: Break a subject into circles, boxes and triangles before adding detail.
steps: Pick a simple object such as a mug or an egg.
Lightly draw the overall shape with a 2H or HB pencil.
Add one or two construction lines to check proportions.
Refine only after the big shapes feel right.

title: Line control and pressure
summary: Practise even lines, light-to-dark pressure and smooth curves.
steps: Draw ten parallel lines at the same pressure.
Repeat while changing pressure from light to firm along each line.
Draw loose circles from the shoulder, not the wrist.

title: A simple value scale
summary: Build five even tones from white paper to dark graphite.
steps: Draw a row of five equal boxes.
Leave the first blank and fill the last as dark as you can.
Fill the middle three so each step looks evenly spaced.

title: Loomis head construction
summary: Use a sphere with side planes, a centre line and a brow line to place the features.
steps: Draw a circle for the cranium.
Slice off both sides to create the side planes.
Add the centre line and brow line.
Place the nose line and chin using equal spacing.

title: Facial proportions
summary: Compare feature spacing using eye-width units.
steps: Divide the head into thirds: hairline, brow, nose base, chin.
Check that the space between the eyes is about one eye width.
Compare against your reference, since real faces vary.

title: Edge control
summary: Mix hard, soft and lost edges to suggest form and depth.
steps: Choose a still life with strong light.
Keep edges hard where light meets shadow.
Soften or lose edges where forms turn away.

title: Layered shading
summary: Build smooth, deep tones with several light layers.
steps: Apply a light even layer with hatching.
Change stroke direction on each layer.
Blend lightly, then restore highlights with a kneaded eraser.
